source.author: K. Maling
source.title: The LISP Differentiation Demonstration Program
source.institution: MIT Artificial Intelligence Project / Research Laboratory of Electronics
source.date_claim: 1959 (Computer History Museum archive groups it among the 1959 LISP memos; catalog does not give a day)
source.source_limit: This contract is a modern bounded formalization for review; it does not claim to be a literal transcription of the 1959 program.

observable_law.input: A finite acyclic expression tree and a target variable name.
observable_law.output: A finite symbolic expression tree representing the formal derivative with respect to the named variable.
rules: D(Var(y), x) = Const(1) when y=x, otherwise Const(0).
D(Mul(a,b), x) = Add(Mul(D(a,x), b), Mul(a, D(b,x))).
observable_law.normalization: No simplification, term sorting, common-factor collection or canonical-normal-form claim. Output shape is the direct rule expansion.
observable_law.failure: Malformed expressions, non-integer constants, empty variable names, cyclic host objects, or a malformed target name are rejected; no host-language coercion.
observable_law.mutation: Neither input expression nor target variable is mutated.

falsifiers: A numerical evaluator that returns only a derivative value at one point does not satisfy symbolic-expression output.
Treating Var(y) as derivative 1 when differentiating with respect to x is false.
Returning Mul(D(a),D(b)) for a product violates the product rule.
Silently simplifying output or reordering Add children violates this dossier's intentionally unsimplified output-shape contract.
Treating a finite-difference table as the same object as a formal derivative is a category error.

dedup.exact_name_scan: Must scan the live D1-D9 foundation and current D10 inventory at review time.
known_neighbors: D10 finite difference / Babbage research is a sequence-to-polynomial reconstruction question, not an expression-tree derivative.
D10 Quine prime implicants is Boolean minimization, not symbolic calculus.
D10 Panini DERIVE-VERB-* candidates are staged linguistic derivations, not polynomial differentiation.
Existing evaluator, list, map and term operations may make this a derived library operation; that is an explicit HOLD, not assumed away.
dedup.semantic_minimality: UNPROVEN — owner/peer review must decide whether this has a distinct language-visible Core law or is composition over existing D1-D9/D10 meanings.

validation_plan.python_oracle: Direct expression rewrite checked against a separate exact integer polynomial coefficient-map derivative.
validation_plan.independent_runtime_oracle: A standalone SWI-Prolog oracle implements expression differentiation and independently checks it against coefficient-map polynomial algebra.
validation_plan.bounded_space: Exhaust all expression trees of height at most 2 using Const(-1), Const(0), Const(2), Var(x), Var(y); then test seeded deeper trees.
